title: Generators and both-persist meetings in ordinary growth
claim: Prove a lasting ordinary source and a both-persist meeting, or a qualified obstruction under named readings with the closest positive, both knot laws and sampled lawful and explosive starts.
standard_statement: For a lawfully growing unlabelled incidence structure, distinguish indefinitely many independent recurring sets of descendants and an encounter changing subsequent production.
prior_work: The ordinary growth operator, the fixed cluster map, two-ring growth and the three-knot unary competition are previous results. They do not establish autonomous repeated products or a later both-persist encounter.
source_contribution: Scope-specific source and meeting proofs, counterexamples and declared reading dependence.

validation.status: Independent in-task proof and physical cross-checks. All seven numerical receipts reproduced byte-for-byte. Program referee pending.

attained_result: Ordinary parity and not-all-equal growth permit a recognizable finite source to emit infinitely many disjoint all-own-parent products, a mixed birth whose two parties persist, and an emitted source that itself releases independent products. In the identified class 7 knots and 25 distinctions are lexicographically minimal for emission and a partner-specific meeting. A 21-knot, 60-distinction pair of preparations keeps both parties and changes their outgoing production. One-step direct timing is sharp and more stringent independent solo replay can fail.
scope: Finite connected lawful ordinary starts, comparison of actual parentage on identified fixed structures at complete size cuts; whole-part and one-step restrictions on complete ordinary stages. All-parent and full physical recognition definitions are explicit. Sharp size is restricted to the fixed-map class with only witnessed pairs and no double witness at its original base, not all ordinary starts. Isolated comparison, full versus weaker reading, and sampled frequencies are separately qualified.
